published_claim.headline: MindSkillEvolve improves success by 9.2 percentage points over the initial-skill baseline.
published_claim.scope_guard: This audit concerns the pinned public SpreadsheetBench skill-evolution path and reported benchmark rows only. It does not establish general self-improvement safety or transfer to O.

observations: The pinned repository contains a runnable SpreadsheetBench-Verified evaluator, automatic Verified-400 dataset download path, a shipped initial xlsx skill, trajectory/evolution event logging, and unit tests for scoring and batched evolution lifecycle.
Pinned evaluator defaults expose model=gpt-5.4-mini, temperature=0, seed=1447, max_turns=15, and --evolve-every default 1.
The server-side skill evolution defaults use min_aggregate=max_aggregate=8 summaries, use_trajectory_score=true, evolved_status=draft, and summarize/propose/apply/mint a chained version.
The FastAPI evaluation client writes any returned evolved version bundle into the live local skill directory immediately, so the next benchmark batch uses the newly minted version.

The official evaluation guide explicitly says the current CLI does not expose the full Unsup./Sup. experiment protocol used by the README table and says reported runs must record actual model, concurrency, random seed, and repeat count.

acceptance_semantics.observed_public_path: trajectory -> stored injected traces/scores -> summaries -> patch proposal -> patch application -> mint draft/cloud version -> client fetches version -> overwrite live skill bundle for subsequent tasks
acceptance_semantics.qualification: No separate held-out behavioral A/B acceptance test was visible between patch generation and mint/staging in the audited pinned code path. This does not prove that an unpublished wrapper or a paper-only experiment configuration adds one elsewhere.

reproduction_status.independent_search_scope: Targeted web/GitHub search for MindMemOS/MindSkillEvolve SpreadsheetBench reproduction, rerun, independent replication, and benchmark issue reports. Results found the official repository, benchmark project, integrations, tutorials, and secondary reviews, but no source-qualified independent numerical rerun of the reported 400-task rows.

reproduction_blockers: Exact paper-table Unsup./Sup. protocol is not fully selectable from the current public CLI; the official eval guide acknowledges this boundary.
A faithful full rerun requires external LLM API credentials/provider behavior plus the MindMemOS service stack and substantial 400-task inference/evolution cost.
The default model is a service model name rather than a pinned immutable model artifact; provider/version drift can change numerical results.
No committed source-qualified result manifest containing the exact three/repeated benchmark runs and all runtime parameters was located in this audit.
No independent numerical rerun was found in the targeted search.
decision_relevant_correction: Treat the 9.2-point result as an author-reported result with unusually good public implementation support, not as independently reproduced evidence. The public code does substantiate that the benchmark path can perform online trajectory-driven skill minting and immediate reuse, but it does not by itself substantiate a held-out promotion gate.
exact_next_action: Search the paper primary full experiment section and repository/release history for a source-qualified experiment manifest or configuration that pins the reported Unsup./Sup. cadence, score-use flag, model endpoint/version, concurrency, three/repeated run seeds, and result artifacts. If recovered, compare it byte-for-byte with the public evaluator path before attempting any numerical rerun.
